sounds.description: Console. A short, soft electronic blip (80 to 120 ms), like a 1960s telemetry readout updating: mid-high pitch, clean, no reverb. 3 or 4 takes, slightly different in pitch, so the repetition doesn't show. Plays every 2 to 4 s (at random), a take at random, softer than everything else, while a camera is live, and stops once telemetry is lost.

Console. An attention tone, not an alarm, short enough to sound three times in 1.5 s (under 0.4 s): a quick rising sweep. Plays when the CAUTION lamp lights: once after a glitch, three times with the lamp's flashes when the controllers save one.

Console. A harsh, urgent alarm pulse in the manner of Apollo's master alarm, cut as a seamless loop of half a second or so, one buzz and its gap. Plays from the reveal of a failure or a catastrophic failure for 3 s, then stops while the lamp stays lit. OGG, for a seamless loop.
Console. Soft radio static with a faint crackle, a seamless loop of 3 to 5 s. Very quiet: it plays under every step without a clip of its own, which is most steps for now. OGG, for a seamless loop.

Console. A dry mechanical click (about 50 to 100 ms): a relay or a toggle switch. Two takes, a press and a release, which the no-repeat deal alternates. Plays on Play and Pause, as the HOLD lamp goes on or off.

Clips. A rocket engine's roar at full thrust, steady in level and pitch, a seamless loop (16 s). Plays while an engine burns on screen: the launch from ignition, the ascent's first and upper stages (the upper one quieter, further off), the retro motors. It carries on from the launch into the ascent without a break. OGG, for a seamless loop.

Music. A short fanfare, about 5 to 10 s, once, when a mission's replay reaches its season summary and the mission didn't fail (glitches, solved or not, don't count). Classic space-age orchestral: bright brass, soaring strings, rising to a confident major-key finish and a clean, decisive ending, no fade. Instrumental. OGG or MP3.

Music. A short sting, about 5 to 10 s, once, when a mission's replay reaches its season summary and the mission failed or ended in catastrophe. Classic space-age orchestral: dark low brass and strings over a held low note, a grinding dissonance that swells to one bitter accent, then a quick collapse into silence. Grave, not horrifying; no triumph. Instrumental. OGG or MP3.
Mission control's room: distant radio chatter and the room's own noise, under the music the whole replay long, never loud enough to follow. A seamless loop of 30 s or more. OGG, for a seamless loop.

"Go for launch." / "All systems go for launch." The launch preparations' success, at its reveal. Radio: a flight controller's call on the loop, VibeVoice in ComfyUI (the user's workflow), brownian noise under it, the Quindar tones at both ends (assets-raw/audio/chatter/). Streamed; it never overlaps another.
